title: Natural shifted comparison of section Hom-complex homology with homotopy classes
statement: On any ringed site with commutative ring sheaf R and object U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], let I′, I, L′, L be arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], s:I′→I and t:L′→L chain maps, and n any integer. Degree-n homology of sections at U of the sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] identifies with morphisms L|U→(I′|U)[n] in the homotopy category, and similarly for (L′,I). There exist these two equivalences for which the map induced by s and t agrees with precomposition by the homotopy class of t|U and postcomposition by the homotopy class of (s|U)[n]. No K-injectivity or derived-category assumptions are made.

source.place: Tag 0A8Y, Equation 21.34.0.1; componentwise composition in Section 21.34

proof.text: Evaluate the product projections of the sheaf Hom complex at U. Internal Hom sections are localized module maps, and sections preserve products, so degree-n sections are families L^p|U→I^(p+n)|U. The differential equation d_I f=(-1)^n f d_L is precisely the chain-map equation into I|U[n]. The degree-(n−1) differential becomes the null-homotopy formula after multiplying the homotopy family by (-1)^n. Both quotient projections are surjective, so their quotients identify homology with homotopy classes.

The chosen Hom bifunctor has componentwise pre- and post-composition by its projection formulas. Thus the map on cycles is f↦s f t, whose image in the homotopy category is precomposition by t|U and postcomposition by (s|U)[n]. The same sign depends only on n, so it commutes with both maps. Pass to homology using surjectivity of the cycle projection.

theorem homComplex_sections_homotopy_naturality
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    {I' I L' L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)) ℤ}
    (s : I' ⟶ I) (t : L' ⟶ L) (n : ℤ) :
    let R₀ := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R
    let E := (SheafOfModules.forget R₀ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.evaluation R₀.obj (op U) ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R₀.obj.obj (op U))) AddCommGrpCat).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    letI := module_overFunctor_preservesZero R₀ U
    let res := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R₀ U).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let Q := HomotopyCategory.quotient (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (R₀.over U))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let f := E.map (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).map t.op).app I' ≫
      ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op L')).map s)
    ∃ a : (E.obj (homComplex (R := R) L I')).homology n ≃
        (Q.obj (res.obj L) ⟶ Q.obj ((res.obj I')⟦n⟧)),
      ∃ b : (E.obj (homComplex (R := R) L' I)).homology n ≃
          (Q.obj (res.obj L') ⟶ Q.obj ((res.obj I)⟦n⟧)),
        ∀ x, b (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f n x) =
          Q.map (res.map t) ≫ a x ≫ Q.map ((shiftFunctor _ n).map (res.map s))
